method: Every actor has one preselected case. Work items identify missing claim-level audit and causal evidence, not inferred influence. A completed task requires source opening, date/definition matching, independent outcome corroboration and documented review. Two cases now include explicitly sourced dated event cross-checks. Completed tasks cover source corroboration at their stated scope, not comprehensive independent claim-level audits. Russia, EU and India now have directly opened dated source confirmations for scoped milestone/baseline claims. Source opening does not establish independent performance or attribution. Five-sphere baseline/follow-up assessments are descriptive research assessments; comparable units do not imply influence attribution. Actor-specific alternative explanations and discriminating measurements are preregistered research hypotheses, not verified causal findings.

items.title: 2023 Camp David trilateral cooperation commitments
items.knownObservation: August 18, 2023: US, Japan and South Korea committed to activate trilateral real-time DPRK missile-warning data sharing. November 2023: ministers reported final-stage testing. December 19, 2023: all three governments announced full activation following operational tests. This is a documented change from prior separate US bilateral data-sharing arrangements, not proof of unilateral US influence.

items.title: 2023 Beijing agreement to resume Saudi-Iran diplomatic relations

items.title: Russia-Belarus Union State security guarantees treaty
items.knownObservation: Treaty signed 6 December 2024, ratified by Russia in February 2025 and entered into force 13 March 2025. Prior to signature, Belarus had already supported Russia's 2022 invasion, hosted Russian forces and missile systems, and engaged in Union State security cooperation. The treaty codifies security commitments; it does not establish that these earlier behaviors resulted from the treaty.

items.title: EU–Moldova Security and Defence Partnership
items.knownObservation: EU–Moldova Security and Defence Partnership signed May 2024. Moldova's foreign ministry confirmed in May 2025 that EUPM assistance included contributions to a crisis-management center concept, cybersecurity agency assistance and equipment; mission began in May 2023. comparableOutcomeObservation.indicator: CEPA preferential trade utilization and product-level change
comparableOutcomeObservation.unit: HS-level trade volume and verified preference-claim share
comparableOutcomeObservation.baselineRequirement: Same-product pre-CEPA quantities, tariff eligibility and utilization
comparableOutcomeObservation.followupRequirement: Same-product post-CEPA quantities and preference claims
comparableOutcomeObservation.missingEvidence: Direct same-vintage DGCIS extraction and UAE/India preference-claim denominators
comparableOutcomeObservation.normalizationPolicy: Only compare within-indicator matched windows and units; do not aggregate cross-sphere outcomes into influence scores.

limitations: Not a representative sample or cross-sphere ranking
Research task completion is not influence magnitude
Unknown or missing evidence must never be zero-filled

evidenceGateMethodology.purpose: Common evidence standards across all five spheres without converting unlike indicators into arbitrary geopolitical scores

required: Dated intervention or agreement and independent outcome measurement
Explicit pre-intervention baseline and post-intervention follow-up with matching units and geographic scope
Credible counterfactual or comparison group addressing confounding trends and parallel interventions
Alternative explanations including counterpart agency and prior commitments
Transparent uncertainty, lag, and source provenance
notSufficient: Coincident post-agreement outcome without a counterfactual
attribution.approvalRule: Keep attribution gate incomplete until all required elements are evidenced and peer-reviewed; no causality implied by chronology.

required: Scope of government or private spending and financing obligations
Separate commitments, appropriations, disbursements and realized spending
Economic opportunity costs and domestic impacts where measurable
Counterpart costs, constraints, and potential sovereignty tradeoffs
Comparable time horizon, currency units and transparent uncertainty
notSufficient: Authorized budget treated as actual expenditure
Export FOB price treated as profit or national benefit
costs.approvalRule: Keep costs gate incomplete until relevant cost categories are independently sourced; missing categories must be explicit.

crossSphereNormalization.principle: Compare evidence completeness and indicator-specific standardized changes, not incompatible raw measures or an unvalidated composite score
requirements: Pre-registered comparable construct and unit for each indicator
Publicly auditable normalization, directionality and missing-data rules
Sensitivity analysis for weighting, missingness, and source selection
Independent validation before authorizing any common diplomatic influence score

influenceMeasurementIntegrity.scope: All five spheres' diplomatic outcome cases

researchReadiness.meaning: Evidence-gate coverage only; never percentage of geopolitical influence or proof of a causally attributable effect

scoringPolicy.reason: Ten attribution and cost gates unresolved; heterogeneous outcomes lack validated comparable counterfactuals and normalized weights.

verifiedActivityVsImpact.rule: Dated agreements, embassy reopenings, exercises, legal budget references and product breadth changes are descriptive outputs; do not infer incremental geopolitical influence from their existence.
